name: snow

phase_0.boundary_condition: The ground surface and atmospheric interface that close the snowpack system

⊢.justification: Void state before any ice embryo forms; the uninitialized vapor supersaturation awaiting first crystal

⊣.justification: Terminal boundary that seals the snowpack from the atmosphere, closing the system to further vapor exchange

≻.justification: Forward morphism driving vapor flux from warm to cold, growing depth hoar and faceted crystals toward the surface

≺.justification: Contravariant descent where liquid water percolates downward, refreezing and reversing the vapor-driven growth direction

⋈.justification: Composition chaining successive snowfall events and metamorphic episodes into a stratified snowpack history

⊙.justification: Identity operation where ice Ih basal planes recognize matching orientation during sintering, enabling selective bonding

∈.justification: Splits the snowpack state into two arms: persistent weak layer (facets/depth hoar) vs. well-bonded stable layer

∋.justification: Rejoins the weak-layer and stable-layer arms; conflicting outcomes fuse to B (both release potential and stability coexist until triggered)

⊤.justification: Touches constructive truth: a compression test or propagation saw test confirms fracture initiation and sustained crack growth

⊥.justification: Touches constructive falsity: the same test shows no fracture propagation, refuting the weak-layer hypothesis

⊞.justification: Holds both stability and instability simultaneously: adjacent slopes show contradictory test results, a live contradiction kept in the forecast

⊡.justification: ROM fixation: the fracture line, crown depth, and deposit are permanent, append-only records that cannot be undone by subsequent weather

phase_2.fuse_result: B-state: both release potential and stability coexist until a trigger resolves the contradiction
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Uninitialized vapor supersaturation before any ice nucleus activates; no snowpack exists
phase_3.true_description: Fracture propagation confirmed: a weak layer exists and will propagate a crack under load
phase_3.false_description: Fracture propagation refuted: the layer bonds, rounds, or fails to propagate in testing
phase_3.both_description: Spatial paradox: the same weak layer propagates on one slope but arrests on the adjacent slope; both verdicts held live in the forecast

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑡: Snow forms a connected granular network where individual crystals interlock through sintering and mechanical bonding, creating a porous matrix with mixed connectivity that transmits stress and heat through both direct contacts and air-filled pores.
⊢=𐑨: Snow exists as a three-dimensional porous medium where thermal, mechanical, and hydraulic constraints propagate through the extended arrangement of ice grains and pore space.
⊞=𐑳: Snow is a heterogeneous mixture of ice crystals, air, liquid water, and impurities where the constituent phases participate in vastly different volumetric proportions and interaction roles.
⊡=𐑷: The structural role of snow as a porous granular aggregate can be continuously melted, compacted, or sublimated into a trivial homogeneous state without crossing a topological phase boundary.
⊙=𐑢: Snow typically exists in a stable subcritical regime where its material properties vary smoothly with temperature and density without exhibiting scale-free critical fluctuations.
